parsed.title: Discussion on AI-driven job search, development tools, and related challenges

topics.title: AI tools for job searching and resume generation

claims.text: The author plans to set up an automated system (OpenClaw) to find vacancies, generate PDFs of resumes, and write cover letters.
Automation of resume generation is seen as beneficial because human reviewers can still analyze the PDF.
AI skills (Cursor, Claude Code, LLM, RAG, Embeddings, etc.) are increasingly required by recruiters in 2026.
The author expects recruiters to become obsolete and HR to become purely personnel management.

topics.title: Impact of AI code generation on development speed

claims.text: Using GPT to generate SQL joins accelerates development by handling routine code generation.
AI-generated code can introduce security and performance issues, such as overly large raw SQL queries that are inefficient.
There is skepticism about AI's ability to analyze logs or provide deeper context compared to a human's accumulated knowledge.
The perceived acceleration of development started becoming noticeable only around 2025, despite earlier hype.

topics.title: Limitations and risks of AI-generated code

claims.text: A generated query pulled almost all user data, creating security and performance problems.
A teammate pushed unreviewed SELECT * queries to production after AI generation, leading to project breakage.
Some developers believe AI cannot replace deep, contextual problem solving that comes from experience.
One participant predicts recruiters will disappear and HR will merely manage personnel.

topics.title: Relation between question quality and answer quality

claims.text: The quality of AI responses is often proportional to the quality of the question and the amount of supplemental knowledge available.

Another participant mentioned undecided generation but noted there is something appealing about the car.
